subject: Amaya: Data retention, deletion SLAs & log retention — follow-up

Subject: Amaya: Data retention, deletion SLAs & log retention — post-call recap

Hi Sofia and Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side related to security/compliance and data retention that you asked about during the demo:

- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type I report available today; our Type II audit is in progress with expected completion in Q2 2027. I'm attaching the Type I report and a short timeline.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support tenant-level data controls, data residency options, and can execute a DPA. Redwood also supports HIPAA-covered workflows and is willing to sign a BAA — I've attached our standard BAA template for review.
- Deletion SLAs: For primary customer data we offer a standard deletion SLA of 30 days from request. Backups are retained by default for up to 90 days; physical purge from backup media follows the backup retention window. We can discuss expedited purge options for backups as an add-on.
- Log retention & backups: Application and audit logs default to 90 days retention. Logs that contain PII can be redacted/hashed before storage on request. We also support configurable log retention for enterprise customers.
- Vendor security questionnaire: I've attached our pre-filled questionnaire (answers) and a blank copy for you to complete. If you prefer, we can start a collaborative Google Drive copy and iterate.

Next steps:
1) Neha from our security team will follow up with a short SLA snippet and BAA confirmation (cc'd).
2) Marissa (me) to share the Drive link and SOC 2 Type I (attached).
3) Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to finalize procurement and SLA language? Proposed slots: Tue 2027-02-16 10:00-12:00 PT or Wed 2027-02-17 14:00-15:00 PT.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeI.pdf, redwood_security_questionnaire_answers.xlsx, Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf, data_retention_factsheet.pdf

Subject: Re: Amaya: Data retention, deletion SLAs & log retention — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A few clarifications so our security team can evaluate:

1) Backups: when you say backups are retained for up to 90 days, does a customer-initiated deletion request trigger immediate removal from all live and backup systems, or is the data only removed from the live system and left in backups until the 90-day window expires?
2) Expedited purge: can you outline service-levels and costs if we need an expedited purge from backups (e.g., within 7 days)?
3) Logs: are logs encrypted at rest and can we request PII redaction at the application logging layer, or would that require changes on our end to avoid logging PII? Also what's the default retention for audit logs vs application logs?
4) HIPAA/BAA: we will need Redwood to sign a BAA. Are there any carve-outs in your standard BAA we should be aware of?

Please loop in your security person and legal as needed. Also send the Drive link to the questionnaire when you have it.

- Liam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@amayahealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@amayahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Amaya: Data retention, deletion SLAs & log retention — follow-up from Redwood security

Hi Liam and Sofia,

Thanks for the great questions — happy to clarify. Below are the security-oriented answers and a proposed SLA snippet you can include in your procurement docs.

Backups and deletions:
- Deletion workflow: A customer deletion request initiates immediate deletion of the primary tenant data and removes the active references. Backups are immutable snapshots and are retained according to the backup retention policy (default 90 days). Physical purge from backup media occurs after the retention window. We do offer an expedited backup purge option (enterprise add-on) which guarantees removal from all backups within 7 days of request.
- Expedited purge: SLA for expedited purge: 7 calendar days from receipt of validated deletion request. Additional fees apply; we'll surface pricing in the SOW.

Logs and PII:
- Logs encryption: All logs are encrypted at rest using AES-256. We support customer-managed keys via KMS for an extra layer of control.
- PII handling: We recommend avoiding logging raw PII; however, if you need us to redact/hash PII in logs, we can enable a redaction pipeline or provide guidance for client-side hashing. Audit logs (security/audit trails) default to 365 days retention for enterprise customers; application logs default to 90 days. Both can be configured per-account.

HIPAA and BAA:
- We can sign a BAA. Our standard BAA is attached (Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf). There are no unusual carve-outs in standard versions; typical items include mutual obligations for breach notification and security controls.

Proposed SLA snippet (for procurement):
Redwood will execute deletion of customer primary data within thirty (30) calendar days of a validated deletion request. Backups are retained up to ninety (90) calendar days by default; upon written request Redwood will initiate a backup purge within seven (7) calendar days under the expedited purge service at agreed rates. Audit logs retention defaults to 365 days; application logs default to 90 days. Specific retention and purge timelines can be customized in the SOW.

Attachments included: Redwood_BAA_Template.pdf (attached), small FAQ on retention and backups (data_retention_factsheet.pdf). I'll also open a shared Drive copy of the questionnaire and share the link via Marissa.

If you want, we can have a short technical call with our infra team to go over the redaction approach and KMS options. Proposed times: Tue 2027-02-16 10:30 PT (aligns with Marissa's proposed window).

Best,
Neha Kapoor
